paragraphs: Decodable Reads sells a subscription tool that builds custom decodable texts and phonics lesson plans matched to a student's skills. Elementary school teachers running explicit phonics instruction are named among its users. Reading specialists working with struggling readers are named as well.

An educator enters what a student already knows and selects the specific skills to target. The student then supplies any topic they want to read about. A planner produces Orton-Gillingham aligned lesson plans matched to the skills a group is practicing. Those plans arrive with auto-generated drills, word lists and activities. Teachers can group students, build individual skill profiles and give each learner independent practice through a portal.

Schools, tutoring centers and nonprofit organizations are listed among the groups the company supports. Organizations are invited to start with a free, no-obligation pilot. Paul Heinemann is the chief executive and a co-founder. He is described as a certified Orton-Gillingham reading interventionist and former public school teacher. Joe de Lorimier is the other co-founder and serves as chief technology officer.
